text: Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Port Ansgar, the company and city officials said Tuesday, ending a months-long search for a site. The £38 million facility will go on 14 acres near the South Quay freight corridor and is expected to create 120 permanent jobs and 200 construction posts over the next year. Work is due to begin in March, with the depot scheduled to open in late 2027. Deputy mayor Elin Wren said the project would “bring long-term employment and strengthen Port Ansgar’s role as a transport hub.” Kestrelline said the location was chosen for its rail links, access to the harbour road network and room for future expansion.
